raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Upgrade vendored DeepEP to 2.1 (`a56d6156febcd9976e55adc85b5155bfac9f28f8`), which includes the upstream NVLink visibility fix, and retain a smaller patch for per-context GIN completion signaling.

## Claims

- Use upstream flush, NVLink fence, and grid synchronization placement; remove the custom deferred-flush implementation. Completion signals cover every allocated context, while arrival-only barriers use context 0.
- Retain the nine-context allocation for vLLM's direct-mode MoE buffers, matching automatic active-QP selection. Hybrid allocation stays automatic.
- Preserve skipped/already-applied/failed patch diagnostics requested in review, including aborting on failed application. Add the NCCL library search path required by DeepEP 2.1's SONAME linking and document runtime-version requirements.

## Validation

**Current revision: build and offline checks pass. Distributed correctness, model execution, and overhead remain unvalidated on this revision.** GPU attempts were blocked by unavailable capacity and RDMA device admission failures (`no healthy devices present ... rdma/ib`); these are infrastructure failures, not correctness results. Earlier performance numbers do not apply to this upgrade, so this description makes no overhead claim.

| Current-revision check | Result |
|---|---|
| Fresh native wheels, CUDA 13 / Torch 2.13.0+cu130 / SM90 | Built against NCCL 2.30.7 and 2.31.2 |
| Patched world/rail barrier templates, completion and arrival variants | Compiled with nvcc against both NCCL versions |
| Linux patch application, byte-exact header, complete reverse dry-run | Passed; patched header SHA256 `1bc42abd841cc6e9ba6c59b68962d7e260e163a750873bd50633f91e89d0979f` |
| Native import and loaded-NCCL provenance | Passed on two H200 workers with NCCL 2.30.7; distributed operation did not start |
| Installer behavior | Seven paths passed: fresh, already applied, partial, wrong ref, broken patch, missing patch, other project |
| NCCL linker-path selection | Passed for explicit EP root, legacy root, pip metadata, missing installation |
| Changed-file pre-commit hooks | Passed |

Build checks used `uv build --wheel --no-build-isolation` with `EP_NUM_TOPK_IDX_BITS=64`, `TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST=9.0`, and explicit matching NCCL roots. Patch checks used `patch --batch -p1` and `patch --batch --force --reverse --dry-run -p1`. Local validation artifacts retain the source, wheel, NCCL, and resulting-header hashes.

```bash
pre-commit run --files docker/Dockerfile docker/versions.json \
  docs/serving/expert_parallel_deployment.md \
  tools/ep_kernels/install_python_libraries.sh \
  tools/ep_kernels/patches/deepep-gin-barrier-data-visibility.patch
```

Before merge, rerun matched EP8 direct-mode stock/patched correctness at 9/17 contexts, representative direct/hybrid operator timings, and the original vLLM model reproducer on this revision. Ordinary CI does not cover the three-node H200/GDAKI reproducer.

<details>
<summary>Historical evidence on the previous DeepEP pin — not validation of this upgrade</summary>

The previous `d4f41e4e` implementation at PR commit `c781de2f82` passed the original DeepSeek-V4-Flash reproducer: DP8/TP1/EP, three H200 nodes (4+2+2), NCCL 2.30.7, direct `deepep_v2`, eager execution. Six rounds of 64 requests completed (384/384); all eight audit ranks saved checkpoints and all three servers exited 0, with no count/slot mismatches, barrier timeouts, or illegal memory accesses. The audit run was not a serving-performance comparison.

The old pristine pin and per-context-only variant had previously faulted. Subsequent isolated controls also reproduced old-pin correctness failures before graph capture/profiling. These results concern the old pin with direct mode explicitly forced; they do not establish that default hybrid deployments are affected or that stock DeepEP 2.1 fails.

</details>

## Details

GIN ordering is per context ([NVIDIA/nccl#2302](https://github.com/NVIDIA/nccl/issues/2302)); a completion signal on context 0 alone does not supply ordering for puts on other contexts. The selected upstream revision already contains the NVLink visibility fence from [DeepEP#715](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepEP/pull/715). The remaining vendor patch signals and waits on each context at data completion, retaining upstream flush/fence placement and adding context information to timeout diagnostics.

The pin also includes runtime-sized NCCL DevComm compatibility and strict-ordering window registration. Builds against NCCL <2.31 require the same runtime NCCL version. Both tested NCCL configurations used rebuilt native extensions. The constructor/combine signatures are unchanged, and dispatch's new optional argument is compatible with vLLM's keyword calls. DeepEP 2.5 removes the ElasticBuffer and legacy APIs used by vLLM, so that broader migration is outside this fix.

This updates the existing PR rather than creating a duplicate. AI assistance was used for implementation, investigation, validation, and this description. The human submitter must review all changed lines and the validation evidence.

---

<summary> Pull Request Checklist </summary>

- [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans).
- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.
- [x] **Design Fit:** Compatible pin update, smaller patch, existing direct-mode QP selection preserved.
- [ ] **Testing and Validation:** Current-revision GPU correctness, model execution, and overhead checks remain pending after infrastructure failures; build/offline checks passed.
- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Changed-file hooks passed; rendered deployment documentation updated.
- [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Current and historical evidence distinguished; limitations and attribution included.
</details>

**BEFORE SUBMITTING, PLEASE READ <https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/contributing>**

**Validation result: PASSED (no-fault).** Updating the draft with results; still not marking ready-for-review — see caveats below.

## Cluster validation of this patch (2026-10-03, 3× H200 4+2+2, DP=8 direct mode)

Same harness and config that reproduced the fault on pristine DeepEP and on per-context-signals-only:

| Build | Result |
|---|---|
| Pristine `d4f41e4e` | **FAULT** at warmup, ~3.5 min after server start (host/device cursor mismatch, impossible token-0 row header → stale raw-buffer row) |
| Per-context signals only (no NVLink fence) | **FAULT** at ~24 min — same stale-row signature, faulting sender was a **same-node (NVLink) peer** (rank 4→5), i.e. the fabric the patch didn't cover |
| **This patch (per-context signals + `fence.acq_rel.sys`)** | **NO-FAULT**: clean warmup + all 6 probe rounds (64/64 requests each), all 3 vLLM servers exited 0, all 8 audit ranks flushed `checkpoint` (not `fault`/`peer-fault`), no barrier timeouts, no IMAs |

Build provenance for the validated wheel: pristine `d4f41e4e` archive (sha256 `322b6f90…`) + this PR's patch (sha256 `fbde7fef…`, identical to `tools/ep_kernels/patches/deepep-gin-barrier-data-visibility.patch`), NCCL 2.30.7, `EP_NUM_TOPK_IDX_BITS=64`, `TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST=9.0`.

The intermediate failure is what pinned the second hole: in `dispatch.cuh`, same-node (NVLink-accessible) peers receive data via TMA stores to LSA symmetric memory while the barrier signal is a GIN atomic — different fabrics, no ordering — which is exactly what upstream DeepEP #715 fixed with `fence.acq_rel.sys` after our pinned commit.

## Remaining caveats before this leaves draft

1. One clean ~41-min validation run is positive evidence, not proof (pristine hit rate was ~1 fault/run-day in production, though the warmup-churn harness faulted within minutes on both unfixed builds; both captured faults were NVLink-peer pairs, and a longer soak would raise confidence for the RDMA/per-context path).
2. No throughput regression visible in the probe rounds (steady ~12–14 tok/s, ITL ~570 ms across all 6 rounds), but a proper perf comparison against an unpatched baseline at prefill-heavy batch sizes has not been run.
3. Upstream issue for DeepEP is being filed separately; ideally this patch is replaced by a DeepEP-side fix and the pin bumped.

@@ -493,8 +493,9 @@ WORKDIR /workspace
 
 # Build DeepEP wheels
 COPY tools/ep_kernels/install_python_libraries.sh /tmp/install_python_libraries.sh
+COPY tools/ep_kernels/patches /tmp/patches
 # Defaults moved here from tools/ep_kernels/install_python_libraries.sh for centralized version management
-ARG DEEPEP_COMMIT_HASH=d4f41e4e93
+ARG DEEPEP_COMMIT_HASH=a56d6156febcd9976e55adc85b5155bfac9f28f8
 ARG NVSHMEM_VER
 ARG NCCL_VERSION
 RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/opt/uv/cache \

@@ -17,6 +17,19 @@ Before using EP, you need to install the necessary dependencies. We are actively
     NCCL, so you must upgrade it before building or running DeepEP. See the
     [EP kernels guide](../../tools/ep_kernels) for instructions.
 
+Builds using NCCL < 2.31 require the same NCCL version at runtime. Rebuild
+DeepEP after changing that version.
+
+### DeepEP GIN barrier patch diagnostics
+
+`tools/ep_kernels/install_python_libraries.sh` automatically applies the GIN
+barrier visibility patch to pinned DeepEP 2.1 (`a56d6156`). It reports when the patch
+is already applied, warns when another DeepEP revision causes it to skip the
+patch, and aborts the build if application fails. A skip warning means this
+vendored fix was not applied; check that your chosen DeepEP revision contains
+the equivalent ordering fixes. Use a fresh build workspace before retrying a
+failed application.
+
 ### Backend Selection Guide
 
 vLLM provides multiple communication backends for EP. Use `--all2all-backend` to select one:

@@ -10,11 +10,13 @@ set -ex
 CUDA_HOME=${CUDA_HOME:-/usr/local/cuda}
 # Pinned in full: an abbreviated hash is not a ref, so a consumer that
 # fetches the pin directly ("git fetch origin <sha>") cannot resolve it.
-DEEPEP_COMMIT_HASH=${DEEPEP_COMMIT_HASH:-"d4f41e4e93602a15e95f55f6ee8df8f1aaa0e4bb"}
+DEEPEP_COMMIT_HASH=${DEEPEP_COMMIT_HASH:-"a56d6156febcd9976e55adc85b5155bfac9f28f8"}
 
 NVSHMEM_VER=${NVSHMEM_VER:-"3.3.24"}  # Default supports both CUDA 12 and 13
 WORKSPACE=${WORKSPACE:-$(pwd)/ep_kernels_workspace}
 MODE=${MODE:-install}
+# Directory holding vendored DeepEP patches applied by this script
+PATCHES_DIR=${PATCHES_DIR:-"$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/patches"}
 CUDA_VERSION_MAJOR=$("${CUDA_HOME}"/bin/nvcc --version | grep -E -o "release [0-9]+" | cut -d ' ' -f 2)
 
 # Parse arguments
@@ -182,6 +184,23 @@ do_build() {
     clone_repo "$repo" "$name" "$key" "$commit"
     cd "$name"
 
+    # Upstream supplies the NVLink fence, but completion still signals only QP 0.
+    # Cover every context carrying RDMA puts until upstream provides that ordering.
+    # Apply only to the pinned source revision; skip loudly on any other ref.
+    if [[ "$name" == "DeepEP" ]]; then
+        local deepep_head
+        deepep_head=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
+        if [[ "$deepep_head" != a56d6156febcd9976e55adc85b5155bfac9f28f8 ]]; then
+            echo "WARNING: Skipping DeepEP GIN barrier data-visibility patch: HEAD is $deepep_head, expected a56d6156febcd9976e55adc85b5155bfac9f28f8." >&2
+        elif patch --batch --force --reverse --dry-run -p1 \
+            < "${PATCHES_DIR}/deepep-gin-barrier-data-visibility.patch" > /dev/null 2>&1; then
+            echo "DeepEP GIN barrier data-visibility patch is already applied."
+        elif ! patch --batch -p1 < "${PATCHES_DIR}/deepep-gin-barrier-data-visibility.patch"; then
+            echo "ERROR: Failed to apply DeepEP GIN barrier data-visibility patch; aborting build." >&2
+            exit 1
+        fi
+    fi
+
     # DeepEP CUDA 13 patch
     if [[ "$name" == "DeepEP" && "${CUDA_VERSION_MAJOR}" -ge 13 ]]; then
         sed -i "s|f'{nvshmem_dir}/include']|f'{nvshmem_dir}/include', '${CUDA_HOME}/include/cccl']|" "setup.py"
@@ -227,6 +246,20 @@ do_build() {
         fi
         cuda_driver_stub_dir=$(dirname "$cuda_driver_stub")
         export LIBRARY_PATH="${cuda_driver_stub_dir}${LIBRARY_PATH:+:$LIBRARY_PATH}"
+
+        # DeepEP 2.1 links NCCL by SONAME, so pip installs need a search path.
+        local nccl_root_dir=${EP_NCCL_ROOT_DIR:-${NCCL_DIR:-}}
+        if [[ -z "$nccl_root_dir" ]]; then
+            local nccl_location
+            nccl_location=$(uv pip show "${UV_PIP_TARGET[@]}" "$NCCL_PACKAGE" \
+                2>/dev/null | sed -n 's/^Location: //p')
+            if [[ -z "$nccl_location" ]]; then
+                echo "Cannot locate $NCCL_PACKAGE; set EP_NCCL_ROOT_DIR to the NCCL installation." >&2
+                exit 1
+            fi
+            nccl_root_dir="${nccl_location}/nvidia/nccl"
+        fi
+        export LIBRARY_PATH="${nccl_root_dir}/lib:$LIBRARY_PATH"
     fi
 
     if [ "$MODE" = "install" ]; then

@@ -1219,6 +1219,7 @@ def _make_all2all_kwargs(
         num_topk: int,
         use_fp8_dispatch: bool,
     ) -> dict:
+        allow_hybrid_mode = envs.VLLM_DEEPEP_V2_ALLOW_HYBRID_MODE
         return dict(
             group=self._device_group
             if self._device_group is not None
@@ -1227,7 +1228,9 @@ def _make_all2all_kwargs(
             hidden=hidden,
             num_topk=num_topk,
             use_fp8_dispatch=use_fp8_dispatch,
-            allow_hybrid_mode=envs.VLLM_DEEPEP_V2_ALLOW_HYBRID_MODE,
+            allow_hybrid_mode=allow_hybrid_mode,
+            # Direct-mode automatic selection uses at most nine QPs.
+            num_allocated_qps=0 if allow_hybrid_mode else 9,
             prefer_overlap_with_compute=envs.VLLM_DEEPEP_V2_PREFER_OVERLAP,
             allow_multiple_reduction=(envs.VLLM_DEEPEP_V2_ALLOW_MULTIPLE_REDUCTION),
             explicitly_destroy=True,
